technical_issues.issue: Kourou spaceport latitude is incorrectly identified as 45.05°N instead of approximately 5.23°N.
A sun-synchronous orbit at 600 km requires a retrograde inclination of ~97.8°, whereas 87.79° is prograde.
Semi-major axis is given as 7171 km instead of 6971 km for a 600 km altitude above an Earth radius of 6371 km.
STK access table reports a mean duration of 580.8 s (9.7 min), contradicting the student's claim of 'almost twenty minutes'.
The text terminates abruptly mid-sentence: 'utilising a large surface area to ‘ and is suitable'.

overall: The mission concept is relevant, but the work is undermined by notable technical flaws, including an impossible prograde sun-synchronous inclination, incorrect spaceport coordinates, mismatched access statistics, and unformatted figures.

feedback.summary: You developed a compelling mission concept for Great Barrier Reef monitoring with well-reasoned architecture and STK modelling. However, technical analysis contains key discrepancies in orbital parameters, launch coordinates, and access durations, alongside presentation and referencing oversights. By verifying core orbital mechanics, directly aligning written claims with simulation data, and completing thorough technical proofreading, you will significantly improve the rigor of your space mission proposals.
next_steps: Recalculate baseline orbital parameters in Mission Design: set the semi-major axis to 6971 km, adopt a retrograde inclination (~97.8°) for the 600 km sun-synchronous orbit, and correct Kourou's coordinates (~5.2°N).
Align Ground Control & Communications descriptions directly with STK simulation outputs to resolve data discrepancies (e.g., mean pass duration of 9.7 minutes versus 20 minutes).
Upgrade report presentation by replacing Wikipedia citations with academic or industry sources, captioning and numbering all figures, and completing truncated text in Mission Duration & EOL.

criteria.C1: You clearly justified the coral reef monitoring concept and single-satellite architecture in the Introduction. To reach Accomplished, explicitly identify the specific operational entities and customer organisations (such as Australian marine research agencies or government stakeholders) who will operate the spacecraft and utilise payload data, supporting these selections with citations.
criteria.C2: You applied STK simulation effectively to design your orbit. To reach Accomplished, ensure orbital parameters are accurate: an SSO at 600 km altitude requires a retrograde inclination (~97.8°, not 87.79°) and a 6971 km semi-major axis. Additionally, correct Kourou's latitude (~5.2°N) and match your access duration text to STK output data.
criteria.C3: Your Conclusion successfully restates key mission parameters and sensor objectives. For Accomplished, move beyond restating design parameters by synthesising how well your design satisfies operational requirements, evaluating mission trade-offs, and drawing deeper conclusions directly from your STK simulation results.
criteria.C4: You structured the report well and included an executive summary. To achieve Accomplished, replace informal sources like Wikipedia with peer-reviewed literature, number and label every figure, complete broken sentences (such as in Mission Duration & EOL), and ensure uniform citation formatting across your bibliography.
